assembly_instructions: 1. Place the Service Module aft structural ring at y=1.15 m and bolt the SPS nozzle throat, bell, and exit ring below it so the exit lip rests on the ground reference at y=0. 2. Add the SM forward ring, intermediate ring, four longitudinal stringers, and three narrow external bay panels, leaving the -X sector open as a deliberate cutaway for the SIM bay and internal equipment. 3. Install the two exposed cryogenic tanks, two fuel-cell modules, and equipment shelf inside the open SM frame, then mount the SIM-bay floor, mapping camera, and panoramic camera in the recessed -X sector. 4. Attach radiator panels between the RCS stations and install four RCS mounting blocks at +X, -X, +Z, and -Z; fit four individual thruster bells to each block. 5. Hinge the S-band high-gain antenna mast to the +X/-Z quadrant, add the square hub, and mount four shallow dish reflectors around it. 6. Stack the CM aft heat shield, tapered lower cone, tapered mid cone, and forward compartment on the SM forward ring, then add the crew hatch, umbilical fairing, and docking probe. 7. Build the exploded CM cabin insert above the capsule by adding its pressure-vessel ring, cabin floor, three couches, instrument panel, forward tunnel, and parachute canisters so the hidden crew systems are legible. 8. Fasten the launch-escape tower base to the CM apex, install four tower legs and eight diagonal cross-braces, mount the LES solid rocket, then add the jettison motor and Q-ball nose cap.

info.japanese_name: アポロ司令船・機械船 (CSM)
info.english_name: NASA Apollo Command and Service Module (CSM)
info.summary: Crewed spacecraft used on all Apollo lunar missions. A conical 3-seat Command Module rode home on the heat shield; a cylindrical Service Module carried propulsion, power, and life support.
info.description: The Apollo Command and Service Module (CSM) was the crew-carrying spacecraft of NASA's Apollo program. It consisted of two mated sections: the Command Module (CM) - a pressurized conical capsule 3.48 m tall with a 3.91 m-diameter ablative heat shield at its base, housing three astronauts and returning them to Earth; and the Service Module (SM) - a 4.52 m-long, 3.91 m-diameter cylindrical stage carrying the Service Propulsion System (SPS) main engine with a 2.50 m-diameter bell nozzle, four Reaction Control System (RCS) thruster quads at 90 degree spacing, the deployable S-band high-gain antenna with four 0.79 m dishes and a central square reflector, radiator panels, fuel cells, cryogenic propellant, and on J-missions a Scientific Instrument Module (SIM) bay recessed into one sector. A Launch Escape System tower mounted above the CM during ascent could pull the capsule clear of a failing booster; once safe staging was achieved it was jettisoned, exposing the docking probe used to mate with the Lunar Module. This scene includes an exploded CM cabin insert above the outer shell so the three couches, instrument panel, tunnel, and parachute bay can be inspected despite the opaque render.
info.contractor: North American Aviation / Rockwell (CM); North American Aviation (SM)
info.contract_date: Development contract 1961; flew Apollo 7 (Oct 1968) through Apollo-Soyuz (Jul 1975)
info.status: Retired; flown on 15 crewed Apollo/Skylab/ASTP missions

parts.name: Service Module Aft Structural Ring
parts.role: Root structural ring of the Service Module; it carries the SPS engine mount and starts the open-frame assembly.

parts.name: Service Module Mid Structural Ring
parts.role: Mid-height circular frame that ties the SM bay panels and internal equipment shelf together.

parts.name: Service Module Forward Structural Ring
parts.role: Forward SM ring that supports the Command Module heat shield and the crew umbilical fairing.

parts.name: SM +X Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the +X clock position; it keeps the SM cylindrical frame visible without closing the cutaway.

parts.name: SM -X Cutaway Edge Stringer
parts.role: Exposed edge stringer marking the open SIM-bay cutaway side of the SM.

parts.name: SM +Z Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the +Z clock position carrying one RCS quad and adjacent radiator panels.

parts.name: SM -Z Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the -Z clock position carrying one RCS quad and the deployed HGA boom side.

parts.name: SM Outer Bay Panel +X
parts.role: Narrow removable exterior bay panel that preserves the cylindrical SM silhouette while leaving internal tanks visible.

parts.name: SM Outer Bay Panel +Z
parts.role: Curved-sector approximation of an SM exterior panel between RCS quads.

parts.name: SM Outer Bay Panel -Z
parts.role: Exterior bay panel on the HGA side, kept narrow so the antenna mount and internal frame remain visible.

parts.name: Open SIM Bay Floor
parts.role: Recessed J-mission science bay floor in the -X sector; the missing outer wall is intentional cutaway exposure.

parts.name: SIM Mapping Camera Barrel
parts.role: Long-lens mapping camera barrel visible in the open SIM bay for lunar surface photography.

parts.name: SIM Panoramic Camera Barrel
parts.role: Panoramic camera barrel in the SIM bay; it points outward through the exposed -X cutaway.

parts.name: Exposed Cryogenic Oxygen Tank
parts.role: Spherical cryogenic oxygen tank exposed by the cutaway so the SM life-support storage is legible.

parts.name: Exposed Cryogenic Hydrogen Tank
parts.role: Spherical cryogenic hydrogen tank feeding the fuel cells, shown inside the SM instead of hidden by a shell.

parts.name: Fuel Cell Module A
parts.role: One rectangular fuel-cell package that generated Apollo electrical power and water from cryogenic reactants.

parts.name: Fuel Cell Module B
parts.role: Second visible fuel-cell package, mounted beside the first on the internal equipment shelf.

parts.name: SM Internal Equipment Shelf
parts.role: Thin internal shelf that locates tanks, fuel cells, and avionics within the Service Module frame.

parts.name: SM Radiator Panel +X
parts.role: External radiator panel rejecting heat from the environmental-control and power systems.

parts.name: SM Radiator Panel +Z
parts.role: Second radiator panel wrapped around the SM between RCS quads.

parts.name: SM Radiator Panel -Z
parts.role: Third radiator panel on the HGA side of the SM.

parts.name: SIM Bay Edge Radiator Strip
parts.role: Narrow remaining radiator strip beside the open SIM bay, showing that the science bay interrupts the normal SM skin.

parts.name: SPS Nozzle Throat
parts.role: Narrow combustion-chamber throat that bolts the Service Propulsion System nozzle to the SM aft ring.

parts.name: SPS Tapered Nozzle Bell
parts.role: Tapered SPS engine bell scaled from the Apollo 2.50 m exit diameter; it performs major orbital burns.

parts.name: SPS Nozzle Exit Ring
parts.role: Wide flared exit lip of the SPS bell; its bottom face sits on the render ground line at y=0.

parts.name: RCS Quad Mount +X
parts.role: Mounting block for four +X-sector attitude-control thruster nozzles.

parts.name: RCS +X Upper Thruster Bell
parts.role: Small conical thruster nozzle in the +X quad, canted outward for rotational control.

parts.name: RCS +X Lower Thruster Bell
parts.role: Second +X quad thruster nozzle completing the visible vertical pair.

parts.name: RCS +X Forward Thruster Bell
parts.role: Forward-facing small RCS bell in the +X cluster for translation and attitude authority.

parts.name: RCS +X Aft Thruster Bell
parts.role: Aft-facing small RCS bell in the +X cluster, paired with the forward bell.

parts.name: RCS Quad Mount -X
parts.role: Mounting block for four -X-sector attitude-control thruster nozzles at the SIM-bay side.

parts.name: RCS -X Upper Thruster Bell
parts.role: Upper thruster nozzle in the -X RCS quad, pointing outward from the Service Module.

parts.name: RCS -X Lower Thruster Bell
parts.role: Lower thruster nozzle in the -X RCS quad, completing the opposed pair.

parts.name: RCS -X Forward Thruster Bell
parts.role: Forward small bell in the -X RCS cluster.

parts.name: RCS -X Aft Thruster Bell
parts.role: Aft small bell in the -X RCS cluster.

parts.name: RCS Quad Mount +Z
parts.role: Mounting block for four +Z-sector RCS thrusters.

parts.name: RCS +Z Upper Thruster Bell
parts.role: Upper outward-pointing thruster in the +Z RCS quad.

parts.name: RCS +Z Lower Thruster Bell
parts.role: Lower outward-pointing thruster in the +Z RCS quad.

parts.name: RCS +Z Left Thruster Bell
parts.role: Lateral small RCS bell in the +Z cluster.

parts.name: RCS +Z Right Thruster Bell
parts.role: Opposite lateral small RCS bell in the +Z cluster.

parts.name: RCS Quad Mount -Z
parts.role: Mounting block for four -Z-sector RCS thrusters beside the deployed antenna boom.

parts.name: RCS -Z Upper Thruster Bell
parts.role: Upper outward-pointing thruster in the -Z RCS quad.

parts.name: RCS -Z Lower Thruster Bell
parts.role: Lower outward-pointing thruster in the -Z RCS quad.

parts.name: RCS -Z Left Thruster Bell
parts.role: Lateral small RCS bell in the -Z cluster.

parts.name: RCS -Z Right Thruster Bell
parts.role: Opposite lateral small RCS bell in the -Z cluster.

parts.name: HGA Deployable Mast
parts.role: Angled deployable boom that moves the S-band antenna cluster clear of the SM body.

parts.name: HGA Square Reflector Hub
parts.role: Central square reflector hub of the high-gain antenna, scaled from the 0.28 m Apollo unit.

parts.name: HGA Upper Shallow Dish
parts.role: One of four shallow tapered S-band dish reflectors, individually visible rather than merged into one disk.

parts.name: HGA Lower Shallow Dish
parts.role: Lower shallow reflector in the four-dish deployed high-gain antenna cluster.

parts.name: HGA Left Shallow Dish
parts.role: Left shallow reflector in the four-dish S-band antenna cluster.

parts.name: HGA Right Shallow Dish
parts.role: Right shallow reflector in the four-dish S-band antenna cluster.

parts.name: Crew Umbilical Fairing
parts.role: External fairing carrying electrical and fluid umbilicals across the SM-to-CM joint.

parts.name: CM Aft Heat Shield
parts.role: Broad ablative heat shield at the Command Module base, scaled from the 3.91 m Apollo diameter.

parts.name: CM Lower Tapered Outer Shell
parts.role: Lower tapered outer shell segment forming the wide base of the CM; its hidden cabin is exposed separately in the exploded insert.

parts.name: CM Mid Tapered Outer Shell
parts.role: Middle tapered CM shell around the three-astronaut cabin; the cabin layout is shown in an exploded module above.

parts.name: CM Forward Compartment
parts.role: Forward tapered CM compartment containing parachute, tunnel, and docking-probe structure in the real vehicle.

parts.name: CM Side Hatch
parts.role: Crew ingress and egress hatch on the side of the Command Module, raised slightly so it remains visible in ISO.

parts.name: Docking Probe
parts.role: Central CM apex probe that engaged the Lunar Module drogue during docking.

parts.name: Exploded CM Pressure Vessel Ring
parts.role: Exploded cabin reference ring showing the crew pressure-vessel diameter outside the opaque CM shell.

parts.name: Exploded CM Cabin Floor
parts.role: Flat crew-cabin deck in the exploded insert; it locates the three couches relative to the pressure vessel.

parts.name: Left Crew Couch
parts.role: Left astronaut couch in the exploded cabin insert, showing the CM was a three-seat pressure vessel.

parts.name: Center Crew Couch
parts.role: Center astronaut couch positioned between the two side couches in the exploded CM cabin.

parts.name: Right Crew Couch
parts.role: Right astronaut couch completing the three-abreast Apollo crew arrangement.

parts.name: Exploded CM Instrument Panel
parts.role: Forward instrument panel in the exploded cabin insert, visible ahead of the crew couches.

parts.name: Exploded CM Forward Tunnel
parts.role: Short tunnel cylinder representing the passage from the crew cabin to the docking probe at the CM apex.

parts.name: Exploded CM Parachute Canister A
parts.role: One forward-compartment parachute canister shown in the exploded insert instead of hidden in the CM nose.

parts.name: Exploded CM Parachute Canister B
parts.role: Second forward-compartment parachute canister paired with the first to expose the recovery subsystem.

parts.name: LES Tower Base Ring
parts.role: Circular base fitting that bolts the launch-escape tower to the CM forward compartment.

parts.name: LES Tower Leg +X
parts.role: One of four slender steel tower legs transferring escape-rocket thrust into the CM structure.

parts.name: LES Tower Leg -X
parts.role: Opposite tower leg completing the fore-aft pair of the LES truss.

parts.name: LES Tower Leg +Z
parts.role: Port-side tower leg making the LES a real four-member truss rather than a pole.

parts.name: LES Tower Leg -Z
parts.role: Starboard-side tower leg carrying the fourth corner of the LES truss.

parts.name: LES Diagonal Brace +X to +Z
parts.role: Diagonal cross-brace tying two adjacent tower legs so the LES reads as a triangulated truss.

parts.name: LES Diagonal Brace +Z to -X
parts.role: Second lower diagonal brace around the LES tower base.

parts.name: LES Diagonal Brace -X to -Z
parts.role: Third lower diagonal brace preventing the tower legs from reading as isolated rods.

parts.name: LES Diagonal Brace -Z to +X
parts.role: Fourth lower diagonal brace closing the square truss bay at the LES base.

parts.name: LES Upper Diagonal Brace +X to -Z
parts.role: Upper diagonal member tying the +X leg toward the -Z side below the escape rocket.

parts.name: LES Upper Diagonal Brace -Z to -X
parts.role: Upper diagonal member that triangulates the starboard side of the LES tower.

parts.name: LES Upper Diagonal Brace -X to +Z
parts.role: Upper diagonal member that triangulates the aft side of the LES tower.

parts.name: LES Upper Diagonal Brace +Z to +X
parts.role: Upper diagonal member completing the visible four-sided LES truss bay.

parts.name: LES Solid Escape Rocket
parts.role: Solid rocket motor that pulled the Command Module away from a launch vehicle failure.

parts.name: LES Jettison Motor
parts.role: Small motor above the escape rocket used to pull the tower clear after nominal ascent.

parts.name: LES Q-Ball Nose Cap
parts.role: Q-ball nose cap sensing dynamic pressure and angle of attack during early ascent.
